packet.title: Casts that keep the string, and the coercions perf-8 left (implementation)

body.p: After (perf-8). With perf-5 to perf-9, SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (sort-once fix, no step bound in the CLI since ) takes 7.7–8.5 s; unpatched SchXslt takes 4 min 51 s (8 min 56 s this morning). left three costs: a cast of xs:untypedAtomic to xs:string costs about 1,600 instructions, though the result is the same string (XPath 4.0, 19.1 casting from xs:untypedAtomic; F&O 4.0, 19.1.1); about 0.7 million single items against unions, choices and enumerations still run the coercion engine; about 0.7 million multi-item values still run the full matcher, some twice when a slice base fails 's whole-base match and is matched again item by item.

item.p: Mechanism: profile first (callgrind on SchXslt's expand stage and tests/bench/coercion.xq); a cast between string-like types whose lexical form does not change (xs:untypedAtomic, xs:string, and the derived types whose facets the value already satisfies) relabels the item instead of rebuilding it; then the next largest of 's remaining costs, measured. Outcomes, error codes and step counts unchanged.
Owns: src/cast.c and its internal header, src/evaluator_function.c (the matcher and the coercion engine), tests/cast_test.c, tests/evaluator_test.c, tests/bench/.

Done when: each change measured before and after (instructions and seconds) in a D-record and the commit messages, on SchXslt's expand stage, coercion.xq and xmark-all; QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 run whole with no outcome changes, case by case. Done 2026-10-28 (): relabelled casts (a cast that keeps the text is the source's cell under the target's annotation), one item against a choice kept by its first matching alternative, untyped items cast without a match. SchXslt's expand stage 52.19 to 47.78 x 10^9 instructions (coercion 11.14 to 6.63), coercion.xq 2.845 to 2.716, xmark-all 8.735 to 8.746; QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 whole: 0 outcomes differ, case by case.
